title: Matrix Profile XXIV: Scaling Time Series Anomaly Detection to Trillions of Datapoints and Ultra-fast Arriving Data Streams

problem.claim: Time series anomaly detection is an active data-mining problem, with time series discords remaining a competitive distance-based technique.

gap.claim: Existing time series discord algorithms are limited to batch processing and scale poorly beyond tens of thousands of datapoints.

contributions.claim: The work introduces DAMP, an algorithm for computing time series discords on fast-arriving data streams.
DAMP computes exact left-discords on streams arriving at up to 300,000 Hz using a commodity desktop.
The approach enables finding time series discords in datasets containing trillions of datapoints.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe DAMP as a novel algorithm addressing batch-processing and scalability limitations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report exact left-discord computation at up to 300,000 Hz on a commodity desktop.
The authors report finding time series discords in datasets with trillions of datapoints for the first time.
The authors state that they will demonstrate the algorithm's utility through an ambitious set of time series anomaly detection experiments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Time series anomaly detection is an active data-mining research area, and discords remain competitive.
Existing discord algorithms have limitations, including batch-only operation and poor scalability.
The authors introduce DAMP to address both limitations.
DAMP computes exact left-discords on fast-arriving streams and supports datasets with trillions of datapoints.
The authors describe planned utility demonstrations through extensive anomaly-detection experiments.

source_observation.claim: The stated limitations concern both processing mode and scale: existing methods are batch-oriented and do not scale beyond tens of thousands of datapoints.

interpretation.claim: A useful anomaly-detection method may need to address online operation and large-scale computation together.

application.claim: For streaming anomaly detection, evaluate throughput and supported data volume alongside detection capability.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported scalability generalizes across datasets, hardware, or anomaly types.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the algorithm's internal mechanism or computational complexity.
The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines, evaluation results, or experiment details.
The abstract does not provide reproducibility materials or implementation availability.
